races.name: Racing To School Haydock Park Training Series Apprentice Handicap Stakes (Part Of The Racing Excellence Series)

runners_data.name: No Knee Never
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here and therefore the key pace influence; James Owen has sent him out eight times in the past fortnight with a solid strike-rate, headgear includes a tongue strap, and he is 21 days fresh — his six-race form string shows consistency at the prominent end, and on good ground over 15f he is effectively racing a trip beyond his recent comfort zone, which could cost him late.
runners_data.comment: No Knee Never won six starts back and has stayed competitive since, with thirds and fourths in between and today's trip and going both already covered. Rated 72 to top this field on a 21-day break, though unplaced last time out.

runners_data.name: Popeye Doyle
runners_data.note: Jessica Bedi's yard is winless from four runners in the past 14 days and Popeye Doyle himself has only one placed effort from his last seven starts; his hold-up style suits a truly run race, but his recent form over 8f-10f on good ground offers little encouragement for this 12f assignment, and a 12-day turnaround on a 0W14-run similar-going record is a significant negative.
runners_data.comment: Popeye Doyle was second three starts back and is quick to reappear, 12 days on, with today's trip and going already covered. Rated 69, he's yet to win in this sequence, but the placed effort underpins him as our pick.

runners_data.name: Tees George
runners_data.note: Adrian Nicholls sends him out freshly tuned from a 19-day break wearing headgear, and his history shows two wins from nine runs on good ground — both crucially over distances similar to today's trip; a natural prominent runner, he is ideally placed to track the leader and should the tempo suit, his durable style over 10f-12f makes him one of the most straightforwardly placed horses in the race.
runners_data.comment: Tees George finished third last time out, having won four starts back, with today's trip and going both covered 19 days on. An eighth three starts back is the outlier in an otherwise fairly consistent recent sequence.

runners_data.name: Bay Dream Believer
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose four wins on good ground underline his effectiveness in this going, with a strong record specifically over 10f and a win in his recent past over the distance band; Kyle McHugh takes the 3lb claim which helps on a 131lb burden, but Mark Walford is winless from 17 runners across the past two weeks, and Bay Dream Believer needs the pace to be sufficiently honest to reel in any front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Bay Dream Believer won three starts back but the last two efforts have been modest, sixth then seventh, and she rates the lowest of this six on 57. Today's trip and going are already covered, 18 days after her latest run.

runners_data.name: Sceptic
runners_data.note: Ian Williams has been in form over the past 14 days and Sceptic arrives 34 days between runs — a longer gap — wearing a visor and carrying strong placed form in his six-race string; he is a true hold-up horse by nature, pushed onto the map in a midfield role because this field cannot place all its sit-and-wait types at the rear, which means he risks racing slightly out of his rhythm and cannot be relied upon to get an ideal run.
runners_data.comment: Sceptic won two starts back, and was second three starts back, but he finished ninth last time out and is back after a lengthy 34-day break. Today's trip and going are already covered, though he rates only 59 in a six-runner field.

runners_data.name: Perfidia
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard is busy and productive, and Perfidia shows the best similar-going figures in the field with 12 outings on comparable ground and a 2W8P record — solid credentials; naturally a prominent racer, she has been mapped to midfield because the prominent berths are oversubscribed, and if she cannot get close enough to the pace early, her ability to deliver a telling finish from further back than ideal is genuinely uncertain.
runners_data.comment: Perfidia was runner-up last time out, and a winner two starts back, with two wins inside these last six starts. He has today's trip and going covered and returns in 18 days, though a below-par ninth three starts back is the blot.

races.paceDynamic: No Knee Never is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only five rivals, faces no meaningful challenge for the lead in a 1m½f apprentice handicap at Nottingham — this is a horse that can dictate at a genuinely sustainable tempo rather than a contested, pressured gallop. Tees George and Perfidia are both natural prominent types who will look to press close to the pace, though Perfidia has been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are more prominent-profile horses in this field than can all comfortably hold that berth in practice. Bay Dream Believer and Sceptic are true hold-up horses, and Sceptic has similarly been displaced — the field carries more genuine sit-and-wait types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear, meaning at least one of them must race out of their natural comfort zone. With a lone, uncontested front-runner likely to control an even tempo on good-to-firm ground over this flat, straight-favouring trip, the race shape decisively favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort, rather than deep closers relying on a true end-to-end gallop to reel in the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Holds Firm
scenarios.trigger: If No Knee Never takes the rail and dictates an unchallenged, honest tempo that is never truly overhauled
scenarios.body: No Knee Never bowls along in front at a pace that suits a staying-on prominent runner, with nothing willing or able to go with him early on good-to-firm ground; horses who can race close enough to pounce in the straight, specifically Tees George with his strong Nottingham form and course-distance experience, are best positioned to capitalise if the leader fades or to kick clear themselves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Overhauled Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fractionally too strong and a prominent challenger picks off the leader inside the final furlong
scenarios.body: No Knee Never, racing at the head of affairs, has been running at 10f-12f recently and may find the extra ground on firm going a stretch too far late on, allowing a held-up or midfield horse to mow him down; Bay Dream Believer, who won at 10f on good ground and has strong similar-going numbers, is the most likely beneficiary from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and the field concertinas, allowing genuine closers to sprint through
scenarios.body: This shape requires Bay Dream Believer or Sceptic to be produced with a well-timed run from the rear as the tempo eases sharply; Sceptic carries a style-fit discount having been mapped out of his true hold-up role, reducing confidence that he will secure the ideal position, but Bay Dream Believer's winning form at this trip and going gives him a residual chance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Midfield Win
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a false pace early then fade dramatically, gifting a midfield tracker an easy passage
scenarios.body: Perfidia, a natural prominent type forced into a midfield berth, would need to find a clear run in a bunched finish and produces best on good ground, but racing out of role tempers expectations significantly; Popeye Doyle has the hold-up profile to emerge from traffic but has struggled over 10f and would need the race to fall perfectly.

watchPoints.text: No Knee Never sets the entire pace tempo — if he is allowed to stride away unchallenged from the start and dictate a comfortable fractions, the race may never truly develop and he could steal enough of a break to hold on; watch how quickly he clears the field by the half-mile pole.

Perfidia's ability to secure a forward enough position is the pivotal tactical question — a natural prominent type in a field with Tees George also pressing, she risks being shuffled back further than suits her, and if that happens her strong similar-going form counts for less.

Sceptic's 34-day absence and visor headgear flag an unknown — Ian Williams often targets horses fresh, but the redistribution away from his natural hold-up role means Donagh Murphy will need to make an early positional decision that could compromise his run.

Bay Dream Believer's trainer Mark Walford is in a 0-from-17 spell over the past 14 days — despite the horse's strong going and trip form, stable form is a live negative that warrants monitoring in the market before assuming his raw figures translate today.

The going report confirms Good to Firm throughout the card at Nottingham — no late softening expected, which consistently suits front-runners and prominent racers at this track and reinforces the pace-map read that hold-up horses face a structurally difficult task.

races.name: Racing Tv Profits Returned To Racing Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)
Watch Race Replays At Racingtv.com Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Double Naughty
runners_data.note: Has winning form over 5f on Good ground but is a genuine hold-up horse shunted into a midfield slot on this map because the rear of the field is oversubscribed; Jack Mitchell will need to find cover quickly in a small 7-runner field where racing out of role is a real risk.
runners_data.comment: Double Naughty won three starts back, following a pair of thirds before that, but the two runs since have both been sixths, with today's trip and going already covered. She's quick to return in 15 days, though that recent dip is the worry.

runners_data.name: Zoustar Dreams
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Soft and 6f on Good recently giving her solid course-form credentials, and Callum Rodriguez is an effective big-field judge — travels in headgear and as a natural hold-up type may find the compact field and single-pace leader insufficient to generate the gap she needs.
runners_data.comment: Zoustar Dreams won back-to-back starts two and three runs ago but has since found only fourth last time out, sitting second from bottom of this field on 69. Today's trip and going are covered, though the 28 days since her last run add another question.

runners_data.name: Starsong
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old who races prominently and has good course familiarity over 6f but drops to 5f here — Harry Davies rides and Michael Appleby's runner is 18 days fresh with strong placed form at this level, making her a consistent shape-fit for a tracking role behind the leader.
runners_data.comment: Starsong remains without a win in this six-race sequence, though she was runner-up six starts back and third three starts back. She rates the lowest here on 60, and the yard has landed just one from 26 runners in the last fortnight, making her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Sound And Vision
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this field and the axis around which the whole race revolves — Ed Walker's filly was last seen 189 days ago and returns off a break, but she has won and placed over 5f on Standard ground and Ashley Lewis (5) simply needs to find a clean rhythm in front; the style-fit tag reflects she is doing exactly what comes naturally, which is actually positive here.
runners_data.comment: Sound And Vision was a winner two starts back and placed again three back, with today's distance already covered. But she is having her first run in 189 days, a big query on fitness that offsets the promise in the form.

runners_data.name: Control Room
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's three-year-old has placed at both 5f and 6f on Good and Soft and won over the trip on Soft, showing versatility — Jack Gilligan tracks prominently by nature, the recent 21-day freshener is not a concern, and her recent form figures (1-2-3) over this trip suggest she is in a rich vein.
runners_data.comment: Control Room was third last time out in a striking sequence of places, a winner three starts back with runner-up efforts either side. She has today's trip and going covered 21 days on, with only a stray ninth five starts back as the blemish.

runners_data.name: Marajito
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's four-year-old has two wins over today's exact 5f/Good combination in her last five runs, giving her genuine credentials — Jake Dickson (7) will have her in hold-up mode and she is the one true closing type who was not redistributed on the map, meaning she may secure her natural position best of the hold-up brigade.
runners_data.comment: Marajito won three starts back but the last two starts have been modest, fifth then sixth, and she's quick to return just 13 days later. Today's trip and going are already covered, and a solid speed figure of 72 adds to the case.

runners_data.name: Storm Call
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has winning form over 5f on Good going, but as a genuine hold-up type pushed into the midfield on the map because the rear is congested, Shay Farmer (5) faces the tactical puzzle of where to slot in — racing wide or out of position in a fast 5f dash is a meaningful disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Storm Call was a winner five starts back and now tops this field on our figures at 74, with today's trip and going both already covered. She's fresh in 11 days, though a modest sixth last time out is the concern to note.

races.paceDynamic: Sound And Vision is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on Good To Firm ground over 5f at Nottingham, she should stride into a comfortable lead from stall four with no genuine pace rival to push her — Ashley Lewis (5) will be able to dictate terms at a sustainable gallop rather than being forced into a breakneck tempo. Control Room and Starsong are both prominent types who will press for early position just off the leader, ensuring a genuine enough pace without it becoming a cavalry charge. The redistribution note is important here: Double Naughty, Storm Call and Zoustar Dreams are all true hold-up horses but the map has pushed two of them into the midfield slots because there are more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear — Storm Call and Double Naughty are the most likely to fail to get their natural position and will end up closer than ideal. This shape — a single uncontested leader setting a controlled pace on fast ground over the minimum trip — strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce in the final furlong, rather than genuine closers who need a strong pace to reel in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Sound And Vision dictates an uncontested, well-judged gallop and the hold-up horses are left with too much to do.
scenarios.body: Sound And Vision bowls along in front at a sound but not punishing tempo, with Control Room and Starsong tracking close behind — on Good To Firm ground the rail-runner can quicken or simply stay honest and last home, and any prominent type handy enough to challenge in the final 1f benefits enormously.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pounce Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sound And Vision ties herself up slightly in the closing stages and a close-tracking prominent horse surges past in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Control Room, proven effective at 5f on Good ground and with strong recent placed form at this trip, or Starsong who knows how to race prominently at this level, sweeps past a tiring leader — this is the likeliest upset shape as it still involves horses racing true to their natural style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flyer Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely hot early and the closers get a proper tow into the race from their natural position.
scenarios.body: Marajito is the best-placed true hold-up horse given she avoided redistribution and her two wins over today's exact 5f/Good combination give her genuine credentials to come through late — Zoustar Dreams also has course and distance-winning form to call on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Shuffling
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution plays out messily and Double Naughty or Storm Call are badly hampered in terms of position and the race fractures into a scrappy sprint.
scenarios.body: Horses out of their natural role in a tight 7-runner 5f field risk getting into trouble when the gates open and the early jostling begins — any runner that does secure a clean run from an awkward starting position becomes a live threat in a messy outcome.

watchPoints.text: Sound And Vision sets the entire race shape — if she misses the break or gets shuffled back at the start, the whole pace dynamic collapses and hold-up horses suddenly have a live chance they would not otherwise enjoy.

Double Naughty and Storm Call are both true hold-up horses who cannot get their natural position in this field; watch whether they race closer than ideal from the off, which would waste their late energy on early position rather than a closing run.

Control Room has strong recent form figures and is a prominent type well-suited to tracking Sound And Vision — if she breaks smartly and lands a handy pitch on the leader's quarters, she becomes the most dangerous threat in the final furlong.

The going is reported Good To Firm for this race specifically (7:00 5f slot in the report) despite the headline "Good" designation — any runner with a documented going concern on fast ground should be monitored closely in the pre-race inspection.

races.name: Steve Yarborough Memorial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Poor Relation
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's 3yo has a mixed recent profile (5-237) but steps up to 1m2f for the first time with a style tagged as prominent rather than natural lead, though the lack of pace rivals effectively makes it the default front-runner; Good to Firm ground is fine and the uncontested lead is a significant tactical advantage, though the [STYLE_FIT=0.93] flag notes it is not entirely in its natural zone.
runners_data.comment: Poor Relation was second three starts back and third two back, but faded to seventh last time out and remains without a win in these four starts. She does have today's distance covered, though a 31-day gap and a rating of just 64, lowest here, are the concerns.

runners_data.name: Crimson Rambler
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with three places from seven runs on Good ground including a recent 3rd over 10f on Good, giving it the most relevant similar-going form in the field; blinkers fitted, apprentice Liam Wright takes off 5lb, but a small-field modest pace on Good to Firm is not ideal for a horse that needs to be delivered late off a genuine gallop.
runners_data.comment: Crimson Rambler was third last time out and a winner six starts back, with a runner-up effort four starts back further boosting the case. He has today's trip and going covered and returns in 29 days, though a below-par ninth two starts back is the one blot.

runners_data.name: Del Corso
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 3yo has been consistently placed (four places from last five) and is freshest in the field at 16 days since last run; Ashley Lewis claims 5lb and the horse's Good-ground form (0W3P from 7 runs) shows reliability without a win, and while versatile in style the first run at 1m2f on turf will be a minor query.
runners_data.comment: Del Corso was runner-up last time out, backed up by thirds three and four starts back, and he tops this field on our figures at 75. Today's trip and going are covered, and though still without a win in these five starts, he remains the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Miss Pretty
runners_data.note: Harry Davies rides this 3yo who won at 7f on Standard and placed over 10f on Good — the step to 1m2f on Good to Firm is within range; cheek-pieces fitted, but the trainer has gone 0/4 over the last 14 days and the horse's prominent style means it will likely be dragged into a two-horse show with Poor Relation early, making stamina the key factor.
runners_data.comment: Miss Pretty was third last time out and a winner four starts back, with today's distance already covered. An unplaced effort two starts back is the blemish in between, and she returns after 28 days off, rated 68 in this four-runner race.

races.paceDynamic: Poor Relation is the lone confirmed pace-setter in a four-runner field and will lead from the front unchallenged, with Miss Pretty likely to track closely in a prominent role and Del Corso and Crimson Rambler settling further back. With no rival to pressure Poor Relation, the gallop will be controlled and metronomic on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f — a distance that rewards horses who can sustain rather than accelerate sharply. The small field and absence of pace pressure means the front two positions are unlikely to be overworked early, which naturally favours horses who can sit handy and produce a measured late effort rather than pure closers needing a strong pace to reel in. This race shape most benefits prominent-to-handy runners with stamina and a reliable finishing effort, as there is no reason for the pace to collapse or for closers to benefit from a strong early tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Poor Relation dictates a clean, uncontested lead and the pace is neither too slow nor too fast, ensuring the prominent runners behind are not underworked.
scenarios.body: Poor Relation sets a sustainable rhythm and arrives at the final two furlongs with reserves intact, with Miss Pretty pressing but unable to generate a decisive burst from a modest pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Out
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Pretty pushes up to pressurise Poor Relation from early and turns the race into a two-horse duel, elevating the pace slightly.
scenarios.body: The increased tempo burns off the hold-up pair before the turn and the winner comes from between Poor Relation and Miss Pretty who battle it out in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unusually strong or the prominent horses fade in the final furlong, leaving a gap for a hold-up horse to finish through.
scenarios.body: Crimson Rambler, who has placed on Good ground at 8f-10f, would be best positioned to pick up the pieces, though the slow-tempo environment makes a true late swoop unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Del Corso Midfield Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Del Corso, whose form profile shows consistent placings at 8f on Good, finds the pace insufficient and benefits from tracking the leaders unobtrusively before a smooth late move.
scenarios.body: Del Corso travels comfortably off the modest gallop and overtakes a tiring front pair in the final furlong, with his course-style versatility and recent sharp prep (16 days) working in his favour.

watchPoints.text: Poor Relation's uncontested lead is the defining tactical factor — watch whether it is allowed to bowl along untroubled in the early furlongs, as any free run at a modest pace dramatically improves its chance of lasting home.

Miss Pretty's cheek-pieces are fitted for the first time or as a return to headgear — watch how prominently Harry Davies deploys it from the gate, as pushing up to challenge Poor Relation early could either suit or expose a stamina limit at 1m2f.

Crimson Rambler's blinkers and the modest small-field pace are in tension — if Liam Wright cannot get a strong enough gallop to close into, the horse's hold-up profile will be neutralised entirely on Good to Firm ground.

Del Corso's 16-day turnaround is the sharpest prep in the field — Ed Walker's 6/33 strike rate over 14 days is respectable, and if the horse is forward-fit it could be more competitive than its odds suggest in a race with very limited pace pressure.

With only four runners, any incident at the start or positional jostling in the early stages could dramatically reshape the race — a small field at Nottingham over 1m2f tends to produce strung-out races where early positioning is critical.

races.name: Every Race Live On Racing Tv Fillies' Novice Stakes (gbb Race)
Racedays For £9 At Nottingham Racecourse Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ablon
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Richard Hannon who has winning form over 7f at a similar standard and finished second over 8f at Southwell last time; 16 days fresh and Callum Rodriguez takes over in the saddle, making this one of the more interesting live form angles in the field.
runners_data.comment: Ablon won two starts back and was runner-up three back, and she tops this field on our figures at 79. She has today's trip and going covered and returns in 16 days, with only a flat fifth last time out as a mild qualifier.

runners_data.name: Woodstock City
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up specialist for Ian Williams, returning after 40 days off and wearing headgear (p); has a placed effort over 10f on Tapeta at Wolverhampton but similar-going figures are thin, and from the rear he needs a proper gallop that a lone front runner is unlikely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Woodstock City was runner-up two starts back and a winner four starts back, with today's trip and going both covered already. He was well below that level in ninth last time out, though, and a 40-day break adds a fitness question.

runners_data.name: Everyoneknowsadave
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter in the race, which gives Jessica Macey's four-year-old complete control of the tempo on Good to Firm ground; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects that its OR-70 mark has been earned in a more prominent role and Ashley Lewis on a 5lb claim keeps the weight low — the uncontested lead is the entire case here.
runners_data.comment: Everyoneknowsadave was runner-up last time out and third two starts back, a consistent profile that leaves him rated second-highest here on 74 despite being without a win across these five starts. Today's trip and going are covered, and he returns after a 35-day break.

runners_data.name: Didaar
runners_data.note: Most recent winner in the field, scoring over 10f on Good going just 14 days ago for the in-form Gihan Arnolda yard (T14: 3/6); a genuine hold-up type, he needs a stronger pace than Everyoneknowsadave is likely to set alone, but recency, course-appropriate trip, and winning fitness make him the most dangerous of the hold-up brigade.
runners_data.comment: Didaar won last time out to end an up-and-down run that included a third as well as sixth, seventh and eighth-place finishes, and he's fit to strike again just 14 days later with today's trip and going covered. The concern is that the win followed mostly modest efforts, so the improvement needs confirming.

runners_data.name: Caelan
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's five-year-old has strong form at much longer trips (16-17f hurdles) and arrives just four days after his last run; a true hold-up runner whose preferred patient style is crowded out by the cluster of hold-up horses in this field, the redistribution into midfield means he races structurally against type rather than from his comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Caelan remains without a win in his last five starts, with a modest fourth last time out and a seventh two back, though a third three starts back is more like it. He returns quickly, just four days on, and shows a strong speed figure of 76 to keep interest alive.

runners_data.name: Revelio
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's four-year-old has his best form over 10f on Good ground and finished second in that context, making the going and trip nominally fine; however his hold-up style is similarly compromised by the overcrowded rear of the field — forced to race closer than ideal — and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) tempers expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Revelio was runner-up last time out but that followed an unplaced effort and finishes of ninth and sixth before that, and he's the lowest-rated runner in this race on 62. Today's trip and going are covered, but the overall form here is modest across his last four starts.

races.paceDynamic: Everyoneknowsadave is the sole confirmed front runner in this six-runner 1m2f contest and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to control proceedings from the outset at a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Good to Firm ground. Ablon will likely track close up in second from the front rank, leaving the hold-up contingent — Didaar, Woodstock City, Caelan, and Revelio — to settle in behind a modest, owner-dictated tempo. The field actually contains more hold-up horses than the pace map can honestly place at the rear: Caelan and Revelio are genuine hold-up operators redistributed into the midfield slots because the shape simply cannot accommodate all of them at the back, meaning their true finishing kick may be compromised by having to race closer than ideal. The tactical verdict is clear: an uncontested, economical front-runner dictating a controlled pace on fast ground at Nottingham heavily favours prominent racers who can sit just behind the leader and pounce in the straight, rather than deep closers who need a true end-to-end gallop to get competitive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Everyoneknowsadave gets an uncontested lead and sets a comfortable tempo, dictating every yard unchallenged.
scenarios.body: Everyoneknowsadave bowls along in front at a measured gallop, and with no rival willing to pressurise, the sectionals never become punishing enough to reel in the leader; Ablon, sitting closest, is best placed to grab second but may not overhaul the leader. A controlled pace on quick ground at Nottingham suits horses racing prominently who can conserve energy through the mid-race and quicken briefly in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Ablon tracks Everyoneknowsadave throughout and produces a superior turn of foot in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Ablon, shown good form including a win in a similar prominent-running role, uses a handy position to challenge as the pace inevitably steadies into the straight, targeting a horse that may be feeling the race late. This shape again rewards prominent positioning and penalises those who have to make up ground from the rear on a course where the final straight at Nottingham offers limited time for closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly honest early and a hold-up runner finds a clear run through beaten rivals in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Didaar, the most recent winner among the hold-up contingent and in form, would be the most credible beneficiary if late pace develops, having won over the same 10f trip on Good ground; Woodstock City also has the profile but both need more pace than Everyoneknowsadave alone is likely to generate. Caelan and Revelio are tagged as redistributed hold-up types racing closer than natural, so their ability to produce a true finishing surge from midfield is structurally compromised.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunched, Messy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems develop in a closely-grouped field and a hold-up type finds daylight late from an unexpected angle.
scenarios.body: A small field of six can create a falsely-run, compressed finish where horses racing out of role — like Caelan or Revelio pushed into midfield — find gaps late; however both carry STYLE_FIT discounts and their chance relies on everything going perfectly against their natural racing pattern. This is the least likely shape given the clear pace hierarchy and is included only to capture genuine race-day chaos rather than as a credible baseline.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether any rival challenges Everyoneknowsadave for the lead in the opening furlong — if Ablon's rider Rodriguez sends him forward aggressively, the tempo could lift and fundamentally change the race shape.

Didaar's fitness edge from winning 14 days ago could make him the most dangerous closer if the pace is even fractionally stronger than expected; Jake Dickson's 7lb claim also keeps his weight competitive.

Caelan runs just four days after his last start and has never raced over as short as 1m2f in his form figures — both the quick turnaround and the trip drop are live concerns for Olly Murphy's hold-up operator.

Good to Firm conditions (confirmed by the going report across multiple races on the card) will place a premium on those who can produce a sustained finish rather than a sudden sprint, which marginally aids Ablon's prominent-running profile over deeper closers.

With six runners and a single front runner, the field is likely to remain tightly bunched through the middle section — jockeys on hold-up horses such as Revelio and Woodstock City may find themselves shuffled wider than ideal when the race quickens turning for home.
